newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil sets Egyptian desert exploration.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil sets Egyptian desert exploration.

text.p: Pennzoil Co on Monday said it was awarded Block E, the West Beni Suef exploration block, in Egypt's western desert.
The award is subject to ratification by the Egyptian parliament.
Pennzoil said it was committed to spending $7 million to acquire 2-D seismic on the block and drill three exploration wells within three years of parliamentary approval.
West Beni Suef is located about 100 miles southwest of Cairo and covers 8.7 million acres.
The northern portion of the West Beni Suef block is geologically similar to the adjacent Qarun basin, where several oil discoveries were recently made.

Pennzoil also said it would start its first commitment well on the North July block in the first quarter of 1998. North July is located in the central Gulf of Suez, immediately north of the July oil field.

It said it would start the first exploration well on the Southeast Gulf of Suez block in the second quarter of 1997. Pennzoil and Repsol SA each have a 50 percent interest with Repsol as the operator.

Pennzoil is the operator of Southwest Gebel El-Zeit, adjacent to the Southeast Gulf of Suez block, with an 87.5 percent working interest. The company said it planned to acquire 3-D seismic on the block during the second quarter and will start its first exploration well there during the fourth quarter of 1997.

The West Feiran block, which lies in the east central part of the Gulf of Suez, is jointly owned with Agip SpA, the operator. Seismic acquisition will begin during the first quarter of 1997 and the first exploration well will be started in 1998. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
